blocks.text: Born in Lelich in western Serbia in 1881, he grew up in a farming family. His mother helped form his Christian life. After seminary and further studies, he became a monk and priest in 1909.

blocks.text: In 1919 he became Bishop of Zhicha and later served at Ohrid. He established orphanages and supported monastic renewal. The OCA recounts his Nazi imprisonment, including confinement at Dachau. He moved to America in 1946 and taught seminarians.
blocks.locator: Paragraphs on episcopal ministry, wartime imprisonment and American teaching

blocks.text: Saint Nikolai died on March 18, 1956, at Saint Tikhon’s Monastery in Pennsylvania. Although the life describes persecution and imprisonment, it records his later repose rather than a martyr’s execution.

blocks.text: His works include the Prologue from Ochrid and The Life of Saint Savva. His American ministry included teaching at Saint Tikhon’s and serving as its seminary’s dean and rector.
